widgets_values:
Create ONE single, uninterrupted group portrait showing all sixteen reference characters together at the same time and place. This is a large group posing for ONE camera, not a collection of separate scenes. Use one continuous athletics field, one ground plane, one horizon, one perspective and one shared lighting setup across the entire 16:9 image. Exactly sixteen characters appear, each once. Everyone belongs to the same close-knit group and looks toward the same camera. Do not make a collage, contact sheet, multi-panel image, comic page, split screen, separate framed pictures, or repeated background sections.

Use the reference images only for character identity, appearance and costume; none is a fixed background plate. The exact identities are: <Picture 1> Leon, with his distinctive face, ash-blond hair and brown shearling jacket; <Picture 2> Jill, with her specific face, short brown bob and blue tactical top; <Picture 3> Kratos, with his bald head, broad face, dark beard, ash-white skin, red tattoo, muscular build and Norse armor; <Picture 4> Michael, with his mature broad face, receding hair, average stocky build, gray suit and pale-blue shirt; <Picture 5> Trevor, with his narrow weathered face, thinning hair, stubble, tattoos, pale T-shirt and jeans; <Picture 6> the mechanical woman in her reference armor; <Picture 7> the woman in the fitted black outfit; <Picture 8> the woman in the pale Lolita dress; <Picture 9> classic Nezha, with twin hair buns, red costume, golden ring and red ribbon; <Picture 10> Doraemon, with his blue body, white face and belly, red nose, bell and pouch; <Picture 11> Dragon Ball's Goku, with black spiky hair and an orange gi; <Picture 12> the gray-furred Totoro with his cream patterned belly and pointed ears; <Picture 13> Sailor Moon, with blonde twin buns and long tails, sailor uniform and red boots; <Picture 14> Luffy, with his straw hat, short black hair, eye scar, red vest, blue shorts and sandals; <Picture 15> Naruto, with blond spikes, forehead protector, cheek marks and an orange-black outfit; <Picture 16> Miku, with teal twin-tails, gray-and-teal clothing, detached sleeves and dark boots. Each multi-view sheet in <Picture 6>, <Picture 7> and <Picture 8> describes ONE woman, so include only one woman from each sheet. Remove reference-sheet backgrounds and green screens.

Arrange this ONE group in two staggered photographic rows that share the same continuous space. In the back row, standing close together on one low, continuous team-photo riser, place the characters from <Picture 1>, <Picture 2>, <Picture 3>, <Picture 4>, <Picture 5>, <Picture 6>, <Picture 7> and <Picture 8> in that left-to-right order. In the foreground, directly in front of them, place <Picture 9>, <Picture 10>, <Picture 11>, <Picture 12>, <Picture 13>, <Picture 14>, <Picture 15> and <Picture 16> in that left-to-right order. Treat these as the front and back of a real group, never as two image strips or separate panels. Totoro sits naturally with his head low enough that he does not cover any back-row face. Stagger the other heads through the gaps. Keep every face visible and individually recognizable; the foreground figures are shown full body, while back-row legs may be naturally occluded by the front row. Use gentle, relaxed group-photo poses: shoulders close, arms resting naturally or lightly around adjacent shoulders, friendly expressions and attention toward the lens. Do not stage separate activities, isolated four-person clusters or separate interactions that break the overall group apart.

Luffy from <Picture 14> must remain present in his red vest and straw hat. The straw hat belongs to Luffy only; do not put it on Nezha or anyone else. Goku from <Picture 11> appears exactly once, and must not replace Luffy or another character. Preserve all other source-specific faces, ages, hairstyles, body builds, costume cuts, colors, tattoos and identifying accessories without swapping them between people. Preserve realistic 3D faces and materials for the game and original 3D characters, recognizable drawn designs for the 2D characters, and Totoro's fur. Integrate them through the same late-afternoon light direction, cast shadows, camera viewpoint and floor contact. Use a single empty running track and grass field, a single distant set of bleachers and restrained bunting as one unbroken background, with no spectators or other characters. No grid lines, separators, frames, borders or new text, letters, numbers or watermark. Keep identifying marks already present on reference costumes and skin.
